title: Amounts Returned on a Lift Ticket Refund
content:
What comes back on a Lift Tickets refund is fixed by the refund basis the product is sold on, of which the line carries three.

**On the unused days basis** the amount returned is the amount committed to, divided by the days the order held, multiplied by the days still unused, less the product's refund fee. The divisor is the block of days the order held, the multiplier is the days on that order still unused, and the product's refund fee comes off after that proportion has been taken.

**On the full price basis** the whole amount committed to comes back, less that same fee.

**On the no refund basis** nothing comes back at all.

## The unused days basis worked through

Take an amount committed to of USD 800.00, an order that held 5 days of which 2 are still unused, and a refund fee of USD 30.00. Every one of these figures is taken for the illustration.

- The amount committed to divided by the days the order held: USD 800.00 over 5 days is USD 160.00 a day.
- Multiplied by the days still unused: USD 160.00 for each of 2 days is USD 320.00.
- Less the product's refund fee: USD 320.00 with USD 30.00 taken off leaves USD 290.00.

Had the same order been sold on the full price basis, the whole USD 800.00 committed to would come back with the USD 30.00 fee taken off, leaving USD 770.00; had it been sold on the no refund basis, nothing at all would come back.

## The form the money comes back in

What comes back is issued as ticket credit rather than returned to the payment method, which is a finance team decision.
